items.title: Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon Review - At the Manor of Madness
Vampire Survivors' New Expansion Brings Evil Content To A Packed Experience
items.summary: Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is a fantastic expansion that brings in great new characters and weapons for only $1.
items.content:

Vampire Survivors is a phenomenon that doesn’t stop giving. Even now, after hundreds and hundreds of hours I put into it, I feel like the gameplay never gets old and there’s always something new to discover. Part of that comes from the continuous updates and expansions that the game gets, and the new expansion is another reason to dive back in and enjoy the game all over again.

Last week, the game had a new expansion release called Legacy of the Bloodmoon , which came out of nowhere to me. It’s essentially the alternative to its Legacy of the Moonspell expansion, focusing instead on the villains. And just like all of the other expansions, it comes with new content across the board with new characters, weapons, and a brand new big stage.

I was quite pleased with the new characters, and felt the weapons were very unique compared to what we’ve seen before. From Malice’s Scarlet Needle that pierce his enemies and stops them in their tracks for quite some time, to Sargon’s three Fire spells that can combine into a crazy powerhouse with flames everywhere, it felt like there was something to enjoy when I’m unlocking all 16+ new weapons.

And each of the characters have a unique effect that makes them worth playing. Most of these effects are triggered in certain situations, like when you’re attacked, your health is at critical, or you revive. One of the characters even get the new passive weapon slot every time you revive past the first time, which is pretty awesome if you can get multiple revives. There are 12 characters in total to unlock, and some of them surprised me. One of them even costs 540,000 gold coins, which shocked me at first until I saw who I was actually going to play as.

The map also has a great balance of size, power up to fine, and bosses to kill. Like the other expansions, all the characters can generally be unlocked by completing different objectives on this map, and I quite enjoyed myself doing so. There’s a lot to experience, and it felt great to discover it for myself.

There’s even a brand new Adventure to enjoy. I can’t say I spend a lot of time in these contained versions of the game, but it is no doubt interesting and cool to have. There are eight chapters to play through, which tells a little story about the relevant characters in this expansion. It’s not something I found myself playing a lot of, but it’s a nice little extra.

And at the end of the day, what makes this such an amazing deal is that it's extremely cheap. The entire expansion is just $1, making it extremely cheap to add more content to the game. This falls in line with the prices of their other expansions, with the most expensive one being $4 MSRP, and it makes it so worthwhile. The pricing for the game and it’s expansions have always been extremely competitive, and it’s hard not to justify getting more characters, weapons, a new stage, some fantastic new music, and a brand new Adventure, for the cost.

If you enjoy Vampire Survivors and like great games to play on the Steam Deck, do yourself a favor and pick up this expansion.

Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is $1 on Steam. To celebrate the expansion, the base game and its other DLC are all 25% off.

items.title: Vampire Survivors Blood Drive Starts for Bloodmoon DLC
items.summary: People can get Vampire Survivors and its Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC expansion free by participating in a charitable blood drive.
items.content:
Poncle announced a charitable blood drive promotion tied to Vampire Survivors that can result in people getting free copies of the game and Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC expansion . This runs between September 2-30, 2026, while supplies last. Both actual donations of blood and financial donations qualify, as noted on the official site , with people able to submit proof via the official Google Form . It is also possible to enter for free by drawing an original ad for blood donations and sharing it on social media.

This charity promotion means anyone who participates in the blood drive gets a copy of both the base Vampire Survivors game and Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC expansion for any of the available platforms. The official form noted people can sign up for a Switch, PS4, PS5, Xbox, PC (Epic Games Store and Steam available), mobile, and Apple Arcade. If you choose a console as your option, you do need to note your region to ensure you get the correct codes. This is a one-per-participant option for people ages 18 and older.

As for proof, someone will need to provide photos or screenshots. If you actually donate blood, you need to note when you went, the organization you went through, and things like your record via email or app screenshot and photo of yourself at the appointment. With monetary donations, Poncle requested screenshots of things like the finished donation page, donation email, or site receipt. People who supply valid proof and submit the form while supplies last will get their codes within 30 days. If someone is going for the free option, they must draw a blood donation ad and share a photo of it on social media with the hashtag #BloodForTheBloodmoon while also mentioning the official site and charitable Poncle campaign. They then use the same Google form or email the link and photo of the art they hand-drew to [email protected] .

There is a charitable donation-matching program in effect too. Poncle announced it will match donations up to $5,000. It also set up a Tiltify that benefits the American Red Cross.

Vampire Survivors and its Legacy of the Bloodmoon DLC are available now for the Switch, PS4, PS5, Xbox, PC, mobile devices, and Apple Arcade. The charity blood drive will run between September 2-30, 2026 while supplies last.

items.title: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is out now!
items.summary: 🔴Legacy of the Bloodmoon Hi everyone! Our darkest expansion for Vampire Survivors is out now and at a special price: one money! (or as low as we could go, depending on regional currency). Yes, the finance team wants to kill me. https://sto
items.content:
🔴Legacy of the Bloodmoon

Hi everyone! Our darkest expansion for Vampire Survivors is out now and at a special price: one money! (or as low as we could go, depending on regional currency). Yes, the finance team wants to kill me. https://store.steampowered.com/app/4781330/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Bloodmoon/ This expansion pack follows Clan Bloodmoon as they retrace the pilgrimage of Saint Baal’Thasar, in search of a paradise lit by (you guessed it) a bright red moon. There is also an ancient manor that may or may not hide the secret of immortality. Legacy of the Bloodmoon contains:
  • 12 new villains friendly characters
  • 16+ new weapons and evolutions, including a FireBall
  • 11 savage new music tracks
  • 1 new adventure
  • 1 new very large stage

Other platforms

All platforms will be on stable version 1.16.100 or higher. Version 1.16.105, which contains performance improvements and a fix to an ability for Baal'Thasar, should arrive on Android and Nintendo Switch by the end of next week.

🔴Legacy of the Moonspell

But that's not all! Our very first expansion, Legacy of the Moonspell, is also getting extra content and, if you don't already own it, it is also at a special price: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2230760/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Moonspell/ - 5 extra weapons - 4 extra characters - 1 extra music track - buffs to the original cast of characters

🔴Version 1.16.100

The game has been updated to version 1.16.100 to handle the new content, but also to add performance and QOL improvements: - Banish: after banishing an item, you can keep using the LevelUp menu. - Quickstart: it now tries to pick a character and/or stage that is linked to a missing unlock - Special passives buff (Operation Guns, Emergency Meeting): they can now be found in ArmaDios and as a LevelUp option whenever they'd normally be available, and even if the player has reached the passive limit. - Reworked several main framework features to improve CPU and memory usage across the board - Fixed some Drowners not spawning - Fixed Gorgeous Moon and Big Fuzzy Fist missing sprites - Fixed some weapons glitching textures when paired with other weapons (eg. Fleuret) - Fixed damage numbers glitching at low FPS and improved their perfomance - Fixed stuttering when the stage minutes change - Fixed purchase of MAX Golden Eggs - Fixed Luck bonus glitching on Chula-Reh and Henry - Ongoing work to improve visibility of interactable objects/layers You can find the rest of the patchnotes since version 1.15.100 here: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1794680/discussions/0/583931105981294494/

🔴Platform achievements

We're trying once again to find a way to add achievements without affecting the completion rate for the main game, but we don't know if it will be possible. Regardless, new Steam achievements for the base game, Moonspell, and Bloodmoon will be added in patch 1.17, scheduled to release before the end of the year. Once the achievements are published, they'll unlock automatically if you have already obtained them in game, so nothing is lost.

🔴VS Soundtrack

The soundtrack will be updated in a few days with the missing tracks from the base game, Moonspell, and Bloodmoon! Legacy of the Bloodmoon ended up having 11 music tracks instead of 8, but by now I think we're all pretty used to content creep 🤷‍♂️ Please remember that due to the legal insanities of music licensing, we are not allowed to distribute tracks from Operation Guns, Ode to Castlevania, or Emerald Diorama. But we're still trying... Well, that's enough of the doom and gloom of Bloodmoon for me, need a nice sunny place to take a break 😎 Let's see what the options are: 🩻- darkest depths of Moongolow -> Vampire Crawlers 1.1 👻- Tokyo overrun by cursed spirits -> JJKRS 1.0 ☠️- -> top secret - NDA - 0.1 ⛱️- Biggus Diccus Theme Park -> Vampire Survivors 1.17 Looks like there's a clear winner! Thank you and see you in the next patch! ⛱️ - Luca

items.title: Vampire Survivors Meets Spelunky Is My Newest Obsession
items.summary: Messhof's latest turns bullet heaven into a neat and chaotic platformer
items.content:
Blood Dungeon Roguelike Spelunkey Vampire Survivors

Blood Dungeon is a chaotic bullet-heaven platformer that will have you climbing up the walls, literally. Your character sticks to everything in this platformer. It takes the irresistible formula of Vampire Survivors and applies it to 2D dungeon crawling for a frenetic and challenging arcade mix that makes you work hard for your rewards rather than letting you just sit back as optimally managed RNG runs its course. For that reason, it might be my favorite one of these yet.

The latest indie game from Messhof, best known for Nidhogg , Fly Wrench , and last year’s Wheel World , Blood Dungeon ‘s pitch is fairly straightforward. You pick one of nine unlockable characters, embark on one of six unlockable dungeons, and juggle over 100 auto-firing upgrades to fight over 100 enemies to complete over 100 quests. Instead of just hopping from one surface to the next, you can crawl along walls and ceilings, hugging them like a caterpillar on cocaine. Each arena has its own theme and design—one takes you underwater while another is an endless well—but the enemies inside and the locations of certain upgrades are randomized for each run.

You get upgrades by collecting blood from the stuff you kill. It might give you a laser beam or a sword that spins around you. Rare charms might let you freeze enemies or zombify them. As you play and die, more stuff gets unlocked, and the builds start to get more exotic. Basketball weapons will bounce between the walls. Spiderweb guns will shoot webs you can then use to climb in midair. Instead of just balancing upgrades that scale with overall survivability, you’re considering which upgrades might make it easier to navigate 2D mazes and dodge the increasing waves of enemies that populate them.

Blood Dungeon is in the lo-fi doodle art style of designer Mark Essen’s previous solo projects like Nidhogg . The enemies and characters exude a combination of whimsy and irreverence. One character is nude with censor bars across their body and moves only by doing cartwheels. A machine gun icon looks very much like a dick and balls. And one of the bosses, a giant worm, is right out of Nidhogg . The soundtrack by Thomas Hoey, who also composed the music for Wheel World , fills each dungeon with its own unique, trance-like vibe. All of this was neat enough, but I wasn’t prepared for just how deeply Blood Dungeon would sink its pixelated meat hooks into me.

Vampire Survivors games are great at exploiting that feeling that just getting to the next upgrade will solve all your problems, especially once you die and it’s game over. Just one more run to get a luckier drop and all will be well. Otherwise you don’t really do much in the game itself other than the buildcrafting equivalent of counting cards at a casino. Some Survivors -likes have tried to solve for that by giving you more agency over avoiding the hazards flying around the screen, but none that I’m aware of have injected what is essentially Diablo -style RNG into the classic, Mario Bros. -esque 2D platformer as well as Blood Dungeon .

While Messhof has leaned on comparisons to Spelunky and the way that you’re constantly scrolling through levels in search of new secrets and unlockables when asked about Blood Dungeon ‘s inspirations and influences, I think there’s a bit of Pac-Man DNA in Blood Dungeon as well. The mazes you’re exploring have an urgency as if the walls are constantly closing in. Sit still and you’ll be got. Move in the wrong direction and you might get trapped in a dead end. It’s only after repeated playthroughs that you start to memorize the larger structure of the arenas and are able to begin making split-second decisions about which tunnel to follow where and what your plan-B and plan-C exits might be along the way when things fall apart.

This is the part of the game that’s kept me coming back. Dying and grinding to unlock new secrets is cool. Getting your favorite upgrade—in my case the laser beam—three times in a row to power it up into a path-clearing nuke is a lot of fun. But the cat-and-mouse chase as my knowledge of the dungeons grows makes me feel like less of a dopamine-drip-fed pawn in the whole affair. I’m only five hours into Blood Dungeon , but unlike Ball X Pit , which made me feel vaguely gross about wanting to continue playing, Blood Dungeon feels like an arcade cabinet I want to spend all week saving my quarters up for until I’ve mastered what it has to offer.

items.title: Vampire Survivors Gets Bloodier and Raunchier In Blood Dungeon
items.summary: Messhof's latest is a Microsoft Paint fever dream
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Giovanni Colantonio Published Aug 24, 2026, 12:00 PM EDT Reviews Messhof's latest is a Microsoft Paint fever dream

Image: Messhof Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Here’s a two-word video game review for you: Blood Dungeon . That’s it. That’s the review.

No, really, what more do you need me to say? It’s a video game called Blood Dungeon . Bless developer Messhof, the studio behind Nidhogg and Wheel World , for giving its latest game a title that tells you exactly what you’re getting with this lo-fi Vampire Survivors riff upfront. It’s like seeing a store-brand cereal called Sugar Balls. No confusion about what’s in that box! As it says on the tin, Blood Dungeon is about as lowbrow as video games get — and that’s exactly what I ordered. It’s a proudly crude roguelike built for a generation raised on Adult Swim. Sometimes, you just crave something that dares to be stupid.

Blood Dungeon is, essentially, Vampire Survivors if it were remade by a 12-year-old in Microsoft Paint. Poncle’s retro pixel art has been replaced by misshapen doodles colored in with magic markers. Splotchy blue birds and disembodied hands roam around 2D arenas that look like they were made from texture stamps. It’s like opening your kid’s school notebook and having the horrifying realization that they are not, in fact, paying attention in math class. That lends Blood Dungeon a sense of gleeful immaturity that I was ready to embrace immediately.

The gameplay follows all the basic rules of Vampire Survivors. You pick a misfit character (my favorite is a nude dude who moves by cartwheeling, the Skinja) who has their own starting weapon and perk, move around a level as your weapon auto-fires at enemies, and pick up new upgrades as you collect blood to level up. Blood Dungeon is a DPS arms race, even more than Vampire Survivors, with an emphasis on getting your baseline power up to snuff over crafting tricky builds. That can make the decision-making feel a little limited, but there’s still room for aha moments. My best run to date had me focusing on upgrades that cut down my weapon cooldowns (reducing them when I was at full health and standing in a spawned circle) until I was killing bosses before they even appeared on-screen. Get stuffed, Bone Dragon!

Blood Dungeon is a high-score chase first and foremost.

If you don’t enjoy outfitting a tiny hero with shotguns and rotating swords until they slowly transform into a mobile murder machine, Blood Dungeon isn’t likely to change your mind — but it might . The most noticeable difference is that Blood Dungeon is a 2D platformer, so you have to slink around obstacles while dodging swarms of enemies. It’s a slight tweak, but one that gives the action a jungle gym energy. You’ll clamber up chain fences, hop over spikes, and swim through water tunnels in a handful of arenas that play with terrain in different ways. It’s a more active variant of the formula that gives you something to do aside from moving your joystick and choosing between three upgrades.

The more meaningful change, though, is the pace of a run. A game of Vampire Survivors is a bit of a commitment. You can’t claim victory unless you survive 15 to 30 minutes, leading to slow-building runs where you spend a lot of time standing around until the tension starts to ramp up. Sometimes you make it to the 20-minute mark only to learn that your build just doesn’t cut it, leading to a fast death. Blood Dungeon escalates much quicker and has multi-tiered victories, which makes bad runs feel like less of a waste of time. The ultimate goal of a level (or at least the way to properly “beat” it and earn a crown) is to survive long enough to beat three bosses, but you’ll unlock new stages so long as you can beat the first one. Every achievement after that is a matter of chasing unlocks and bragging rights.

Image: Messhof The inclusion of online leaderboards signals that Blood Dungeon is a high-score chase first and foremost. Beating a level is fun and all, but obliterating your friends’ bone count and rubbing it in their face is the real reward. I got competitive — okay, toxic — during my few weeks with it, sending screenshots of my scores to friends who were also reviewing it to taunt them. (In my defense, I beat their asses so goddamn bad, dude.)

Also, did I mention that the name of the game is fucking Blood Dungeon ? That’s pretty crucial.

Even though I’ve played plenty of games that are similar to Vampire Survivors , like Megabonk and Brotato , the quicker pace of Blood Dungeon finally helped me understand why I’m so drawn to the format. Vampire Survivors feels like a modern arcade game. I can imagine walking up to a cabinet with a handful of quarters and trying to see how far I can get in a run, as I still do with Ms. Pac-Man anytime I find it in the wild. Plenty of roguelikes fit that description, but Vampire Survivors stands apart by being squarely focused on a streamlined style of play that’s easy to learn and hard to master. It subtracts where so many of its peers pile more systems on top of the ones popular games have established; Vampire Survivors is more a continuation of Asteroids than Hades .

Blood Dungeon fully leans into that philosophy. I love firing it up for a single run, rather than compulsively sitting with it for hours on end. I set a new high with a build that involves a basketball and two Desert Eagles, and then turn it off and return the next time I’m bored to see if any of my sorry ass friends have managed to beat me. (Fat chance!) It only took me around six hours to properly clear each level and nab over 50% of the unlocks. Great! Now it sits permanently installed on my Steam Deck like Space Invaders on a multicab. I know I’ll get the urge to fire it up on a lazy Sunday.

Image: Messhof That’s not to say that it’s an elevated take on Vampire Survivors that revolutionizes the “Bullet heaven” subgenre. Blood Dungeon is a shallow riff on the formula. There are a lot of toys to experiment with, but there’s not too much depth. There are only a few levels in the game currently, and at least one of them is a dud. (Trying to fend off enemies underwater while grabbing oxygen bubbles to stay alive? No thanks!) It can feel like a quick prototype for a bigger idea, a Hail Mary thrown by Messhof to nab a hit in the wake of its more ambitious Wheel World .

It will either find its audience or it won’t. And its audience is people who see the name Blood Dungeon and think, “haha, hell yeah.” And brother, as someone who is squarely in that group of Neanderthals, let me tell you that it’s hitting the spot. Shotgun shoot 13 shells at skeleton head. Big sword go spin. Ha ha. Blood good, want more blood.

items.title: How Vampire Survivors became Vampire Crawlers: Six lessons from building a game based on another developer's IP
items.summary: Nosebleed Interactive's Andreas Firnigl on crafting a spin-off of Poncle's smash hit: pub prototypes, shared rules, last-minute changes and more
items.content:
Nosebleed Interactive's Andreas Firnigl on crafting a spin-off of Poncle's smash hit: pub prototypes, shared rules, last-minute changes and more

Image credit: Nosebleed Interactive/Poncle Academy by Andreas Firnigl CEO, Nosebleed Interactive Published on Aug. 10, 2026, 3:19 p.m. Follow Nosebleed Interactive Andreas Firnigl started his career as a tester on Big Mutha Truckers, way back on Gamecube. He founded Nosebleed Interactive almost 15 years ago as CEO and creative director.

In 2023, an old contact I had worked with 15 years ago – and who is now at Poncle – came to us with the amazing opportunity to collaborate on a Vampire Survivors spin-off.

Luca Galante, the creator of Vampire Survivors, had come up with the idea for a card game spin-off and had already developed an early prototype, but Poncle wanted an external studio to help turn it into a complete game. So lead designer Luke Wintflint and I worked with Luca and Poncle to evolve that idea into what became Vampire Crawlers.

After 15 years making games and working with other studios, Nosebleed Interactive has learnt a lot about how to treat someone else's IP and how to collaborate with external partners. We learnt even more on Crawlers, and I want to share some key lessons that you can take away and apply at your own studio.

Naturally, understanding the IP you are working on is vital. Yet it's even more important to demonstrate to the client that you understand it.

I've put a stupid amount of hours into Vampire Survivors in order to understand all the little nuances and tics that most people won't notice. This kind of intense playing helps you to understand what is changeable and what is not. Some things will be fundamental to the experience and will have to be incorporated, while others are things that, frankly, players don't care about all that much. Knowing what can and can't be changed is a sign you are working on something you understand, rather than doing a half-arsed superficial imitation.

The fundamentals of Vampire Crawlers came together very quickly. A pen and paper version that we played in the pub during the early days of development was surprisingly close to the final game. However, in those early months, we paid less attention to the IP and were instead focused on adding content, throwing in random stuff willy-nilly as a placeholder. We knew it would be quick and easy to fix later on, and knew enough about the IP to do it right – but Poncle didn't.

We had the bones of a great game, but it wasn't clear to Poncle that we had a good Vampire Survivors game. So we downed tools on everything else and focused on fixing that – making sure all the names were right, matching up how stats would transfer from Survivors to Crawlers, and so on. As soon as Poncle saw the next build, they gave us the green light.

In short, do that work of understanding your partner's IP – but make sure you show them you have that understanding, too.

Fans of the IP will naturally be interested in playing your new game, but you also need to make sure it works for people who don't know the original title. This is why it's important to get feedback from people who haven't played the IP at all.

There were a couple of people at Nosebleed who hadn't played Vampire Survivors, and rather than encouraging them to try the game, we asked them to avoid playing it at all. Having some folks on the team who are coming in clean, as it were, was a real help to balance the onboarding, which is so important in this kind of game. Relying too much on knowledge of the existing IP could make it less attractive to new players.

Your partner is working with you because you have something to bring to the table (there's certainly a lot of Nosebleed's DNA in Vampire Crawlers). So lean into your strengths – but be humble. Be prepared to learn from how your partner works, and what works for their IP.

Before Crawlers, we'd just come off Arcade Paradise, where the density of every pixel had to be exactly correct. Would Poncle do that? No.

items.title: Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton
items.summary: Hi everyone, we have a lot happening around new games and Vampire Survivors, so here's a gigantic news post! 🟣- Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton 🔴- Vampire Survivors 1.15 🔴- Legacy of the Bloodmoon teasers 🔴- Legacy of the Moonspell in
items.content:
Hi everyone, we have a lot happening around new games and Vampire Survivors, so here's a gigantic news post! 🟣- Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton 🔴- Vampire Survivors 1.15 🔴- Legacy of the Bloodmoon teasers 🔴- Legacy of the Moonspell info 🔴- Workshop Support for Vampire Survivors 🔴- ARG and Character Community Challenge winners 🔴- Vampire Survivors Comics 🔵- Vampire Crawlers updates 🟢- PoncleUp

🟣 Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton

A few days back we announced Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton in collaboration with Shueisha Games! Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game like Vampire Survivors, but with a twist: you'll be able to play an 8-player survivors royale PvPvE mode! Some in-game names and terminology are still in development and may be subject to change. While every player plays in their own world, you accumulate points by defeating curses and sorcerers, and with every 100 points accumulated you get to choose a Rule Change that can affect everyone's game. Some Rule Changes are INSANE, but for now we'll just reveal the simple ones you can see in the trailer (silence, slow, steal points...). But Rule Changes aren't the only way to interact with other players. Introducing a world first, mind blowing, unbelievable game mechanic: PRESS A BUTTON. While you move your auto-attacking character, your special attack also builds up. By PRESSING A BUTTON when the special attack is ready, you get to unleash your character's Special Attack, or, if that character can, a DOMAIN EXPANSION! Other players can be caught in the effect of your Domain or Special Attack, so you have to keep an eye on other players' position and special-bar status. A very important aspect of the 8-players mode is the Live Match Status Feed (working name). This big chunk of UI on the left side of the screen constantly updates in real time, acting not only as a scoreboard, but also sending out warnings and all kind of information about what the other players are up to. At the end of the 15 minutes battle royale, the 2 players with the most points will face one another in a 19 seconds duel. Despite the online focus, Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble: Survivaton is a game you can also play alone, in a mission-based mode, just like Vampire Survivors. If you don't ever want to go online, you'll still be able to play the 8-players battle royale mode against bots. This is a game you buy once and can play anytime. We'll keep supporting the game after launch, with our usual style of content updates. So forget about gatcha elements or a forever-evolving PvP meta keeping your time and wallet hostages: our focus here are fun and affordability. Apologies if you had enough of this wall of text, but I kepty mouth shut for almost two years and I haven't even got to the technical bits yet! Yes, the game runs on the Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton framework, so you can expect that same familiar experience playing it, but we had to do several unique tweaks for Jujutsu Kaisen Rumble Survivaton. Other than the obvious, completely new networking for the gameplay and Live Match Status Feed, we have doubled the resolution at which the game runs. That allowed us to completely rebuild the whole VFX pipeline so that we could re-create the distinctive look of Curse Energy and the changes the whole stage depending on activated Domain Expansions or Special Attacks. Another reason to double the resolution was to properly display the UI (that has been completely reworked at framework level) and the Live Match Status Feed, that is capable of also streaming gameplay snippets from other online players. You'll see a lot of other tweaks, like the fact that characters look different if they are seen from the left or from the right, a "default attack" per character that triggers without any weapon, or walls that are actually solid to name a few. Then there are other changes that won't be noticeable until you get to play the game. For example, while we are going by the same content-unlock-philosophy as Vampire Survivors, we are completely reworking the progression in the various game modes and also per-character, so that every game mode will feel fresh even to VS veterans. That's all for now, I hope you have enjoyed the trailer; my favourite part was that bit were Gojo takes a walk.

🔴 Vampire Survivors 1.15 available on all platforms

- Nintendo Switch 1 and 2 - Android - iOS & Apple Arcade - PS4 and PS5 - Xbox - EGS In the following weeks there will be small updates quite often on all platforms to bring them all on the same version, because all platforms have the same content, but not the same bugfixes and tweaks. Please join the Discord or keep an eye on the Updates version of the wiki if you're interested in knowing the fixes in each update (I won't spam Steam News every week for small tweaks).

🔴 New Moonspell Content spoilers

When we'll launch Legacy of the Bloodmoon, we'll also update the contents of Legacy of the Moonspell. It will get 7 new unlocks, that will deliver:

  • 4 new weapons: LunarMight, LunarSight, LunarBight, and LunarFlight [/*]
  • 1 Special Evolution: Argent Flow [/*]
  • 1 new passive Weapon: Pearl Magatama [/*]
  • 4 new characters [/*]
  • 1 new music track [/*]
  • some buffs to the original cast of characters: [/*]
- Menya Moonspell gets Overheal +16: activates her starting weapon. - Babi-Onna gets Overheal +16: gains a temporary bonus to MoveSpeed (that also means she attacks faster). - Megalo Menya Moonspell gets Overheal +16: activates her first weapon. - Megalo Syuuto Moonspell gets Overheal +16: equipped Blood weapons gain extra damage. - McCoy-Oni gets Overheal +16: gains a Reroll. - Gav'Et-Oni gets \.This will be a free update, in fact last month we have actually dropped the price of Legacy of the Moonspell to balance out a bit the cost/content ratio of the various expansions.

🔴 Bloodmoon character tease

Legacy of the Bloodmoon is almost complete and we will be able to start testing and submissions soon! That means we'll have an actual release date soon too. In the meantime, here's a Character Spotlight video about Malice Bloodmoon:

🔴 ARG and Community Character Competition winners

Congratulations to the trio of winners of the Lucca Comics ARG: Jenoss, Miryel, Siming, and GIU_LLS (:poemg:?), and to DissonantSynth for winning the Community Challenge! We're finally getting into the design stage of the characters, with a first implementation that will soon be shared with the winners, behind the scenes, to start iterating together on gameplay mechanics. You can expect a few surprises and little extras about them when they'll make their appearance in the game! Baron Husker and Sefi Rotto (:poemg:?) will come alive in a later update, v1.17

🔴 First steps for Steam Workshop support

Instead of waiting the conclusion of the current cycles of updates for Vampire Survivors as originally planned, we will develop modding support over time, one feature at a time. Feature 1 will be about adding CUSTOM (private/local) and WORKSHOP (public/Steam Workshop) characters! Please join the Discord or use the public-beta forum if you're interested in trying out custom characters before they go live on the main branch, in a future update (currently aiming for v1.17)

🔴 Vampire Survivors Comics

Vampire Survivor is getting comics! We've been working with Titan Comics on a 4-issue series, written by David Hazan and illustrated by Jimm Kucaj, with the first issue coming out this September, available in 3 cover variants. Some familiar Vampire Survivors will go through Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, and a few other places, and there might even be some lore in there. Issue #1 is available to pre-order from your local comic shop or from Forbidden Planet if you're in the UK / EU. You can find out more about the comics on the Titan Comics website.

🔵 Vampire Crawlers: first QOL update

Our first update to Vampire Crawlers add an Endless mode and several QOL improvements! You can find more details, the strategy behind future updates, and some content spoilers in the Steam News here.

🟢 Countup to the next announcement

Look, we're doing a lot of stuff across several small teams. I'm always happy to write the Steam News but I cannot bombard your feed with everything we're doing. Also took me something like 3 weeks to set this all up. So if you'd like to hear about what we're doing a bit more often, then please visit poncleup.com to see a recap or subscribe to our newsletter. It's a countup instead of a countdown because, as you might have noticed, we're release-date-averse and have no idea ourselves when we'll drop something new 🤷‍♂️ Just know that the newsletters are written by the marketing team :vsskull: Alright, I'm done with work, time to go back having fun on my secret project. Thank you everyone, I'll leave you in the self-proclaimed capable hands of the marketing team! - Luca

items.title: Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is coming this summer!
items.summary: Hi everyone! As anticipated several months ago, we’ve been working on several core systems of VS to be able to keep making more content, increase stability, and improve performance. It’s been a while so we have quite a few things to cover t
items.content:
Hi everyone! As anticipated several months ago, we’ve been working on several core systems of VS to be able to keep making more content, increase stability, and improve performance. It’s been a while so we have quite a few things to cover today: - a new expansion for VS - a new update - a new poncle team in Japan - the very sensible reason why Vampire Survivors has a sub-title now 🤷‍♂️

Vampire Survivors Update 1.15 (The Wet One) is out now on Steam!

You can find all details about 1.15 below, now here’s a stupid summer trailer about it:

Major QOL improvements

  • Multiple Save Slots (about time!)
  • Character Setup panel for skins, egg selection, etc…
  • Content filters in Character Selection and Unlocks menu
  • Stability improvements for late game and low-end platforms
  • Reduced loading times (more noticeable on other platforms than PC)

New content

  • 1 New Stage: The Lycaeum
  • 2 New Characters
  • either 2 or 10 new weapons 🤷‍♂️
  • 3 New Darkanas
  • 1 New Music Track
  • 3 new Relics, of which 1 Secret rather than Unlockable

Other tweaks and features

  • "Random LevelUp" can now be toggled during a run if it is already unlocked on the Stage menu
  • Added option to Unbanish a weapon when picking it up from the stage
  • Buffed a few weapons like Magi-Stone and Mille Bolle Blu
  • Rendering fixes for a few weapons, including birds, Prismatic Missile, Runetracer…
Patch 1.15 will be released on all other platforms a bit later, by the end of the month, due to platform-specific optimizations and differences in save slots management. On the bright side, we will also be releasing a Nintendo Switch 2 version, with better performance and mouse support!

Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is coming Summer 2026

https://store.steampowered.com/app/4781330/Vampire_Survivors_Legacy_of_the_Bloodmoon/ Vampire Survivors: Legacy of the Bloodmoon is our “accidental” next expansion and the evil twin to Legacy of the Moonspell. The original plan was just to make a little content update to Legacy of the Moonspell. Since it’s the first and smallest VS expansion, it felt right to try to balance its value a little. Needless to say, ideas started to flow and everything spiraled into a much bigger project. I’m not sure I’ll ever learn at this stage. In the end, Legacy of the Moonspell will be getting its content buff (7 new unlocks) and Legacy of the Bloodmoon will live a life of its own. This expansion pack follows Clan Bloodmoon as they retrace the pilgrimage of Saint Baal’Thasar, in search of a paradise lit by (you guessed it) a bright red moon. There is also an ancient manor that may or may not hide the secret of immortality. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will contain:
  • 12 new villains friendly characters
  • 16+ new weapons and evolutions, including a FireBall
  • 8 savage new music tracks
  • 1 new adventure
  • 1 new very large stage
  • Interesting bits and bobs I won’t spoil at this time
But there’s more. Legacy of the Bloodmoon will cost approximately 1 money (0.99 USD), and Legacy of the Moonspell will receive a price cut and also be priced 1 money :) You can find all details about Legacy of the Bloodmoon below, now here’s a villainous trailer about it:

Vampire Survivors - First Survivaton

Among the many projects we’re working on (approximately 15 projects, not 15 games, please don’t panic) there is also a lineup of Survivaton games. It’s definitely a meaningful word that means “survive a ton” and nothing else. These are games like Vampire Survivors, developed internally at poncle, tied to IPs that might need unique game mechanics, a different graphic style, or are so expansive that ultimately deserve their own standalone game (compared to making a DLC for VS). I’d love to make examples, but I’d have to spoil way too much. Being developed internally, we’ll be able to guarantee affordability and worthwhile titles. Since a good 90% of global VS players aren’t reached by the Steam news (or are not interested in gaming news in general), the best way to also let them know that the Survivatons are tied directly to VS is to also call VS a Survivaton, hence the new sub-title. Please note there’s a dash before First Survivaton instead of a semi-colon, because DLCs exist... The next time I name a game I’ll remember to not use something as generic as “Monster Hunter” as inspiration please know I love Monster Hunter 💌

poncle Japan

We can finally say we are building poncle Japan! It will be poncle, but in Japan. The new studio is headed by Sawaki Takeyasu, known for his work on Devil May Cry, Ōkami, and El Shaddai: Ascension of the Metatron. Having a studio in Japan will simplify and speed up the work we do with all our Japanese partners, and also bring new opportunities for collabs. It’s too soon to say what the team will be working on; we are planning to fully open the studio by the end of 2026. Now it's time for all the FAQs and info blocks, thanks for reading and waiting patiently for this update! - Luca

Legacy of the Bloodmoon FAQs

When does it release? Summer 2026. What do you define as summer? Not winter. How much does it cost? Around £0.95, with regional pricing varying by platform and country. Why will Legacy of the Moonspell’s price change too? It felt right to adjust the price so that it’s more balanced compared to the amount of content of the other expansions. Please note that some stores have minimum prices in certain countries. In some places, Moonspell was already too cheap to make it cheaper. What about Tides of the Foscari then? Please at least wait for Moonspell and Bloodmoon before asking for more, we know we know 😭 Will Moonspell get new content too? Yes, 7 new unlocks for a few more weapons and characters. Is Vampire Survivors still getting free updates? Yes of course, there’s still plenty on the roadmap.

Update 1.15 Full spoilers

♫ Murder on the Seafloor Composed and arranged by Filippo Vicarelli.

Quick content guide:

  • Collect a total of 50 Vacuums to unlock The Lycaeum stage
  • Find the Penshin Fatcha in The Lycaeum and see all its evolutions to unlock it permanently
  • Survive 20 minutes in The Lycaeum to unlock Para Kooleo
  • Trigger a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo to unlock Darkana VIII - Edge of the Earth
  • Buy the Survarocchi at the top of The Lycaeum to unlock them for any character
  • Buy the Green Eyes Vizard at the top of The Lycaeum to be able to find Bat Dragons in other stages
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon (Currently available in Mad Forest and Il Molise) to unlock the Unearthly Bolt wea;on
  • Evolve the Unearthly Bolt with a maxed Tirajisú to unlock Big Troubler
  • Defeat any Bat Dragon with Big Troubler and Arcana 0 - Game Killer to unlock Darkana 0 - Stake to your Heart
  • Survive 15 minutes in Inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups to unlock Darkana XIX - Heir of Fate
  • Defeat 2 unique Bat Dragons to unlock a new set of Survarots to purchase from Big Troubler

Detailed info

New stage: The Lycaeum An underwater-themed stage where you press some buttons, beat some crabs, run to the center, kill more things, press more buttons, don’t die. The Drowner can only be defeated via raw damage or by reaching the top of the stage. Hidden treasures can be collected only using Mad Groove or Lavatrix Machina. Teleporters become active after reaching the top once. New character: Para Kooleo Starts with a Move Speed and Duration bonus. When his HP drops below a certain threshold it triggers a Vacuum. He also likes to evolve weapons. He has an abundance of skins. New character: Big Troubler Loves gold and gets trigger happy when he gets gold. The gold also loves him and will protect him at all costs. New weapon: Penshin Fatcha & Tonno Subito / Tonnado / Tonn’omoto / Tonn’oddeeo / Tonne / Unsurpassed / Miracle of Multiplication. Starting weapon for Para Kooleo. Select one of six tuna forms. Evolve it from one to another, stacking stats as you go. Evolve at least once to transform all the Vacuums pickup into "Lavatrix Machina". Then, if you choose to, evolve into the secret evolution, Miracle of Multiplication where everything happens at once. Does not require any items to evolve, but many, many treasure chests. New weapon: Unearthly Bolt & Spirit Disturbance Starting weapon of Big Troubler. Spawns green bolts that attack the closest enemy. It deals increasingly high damage if it Crits in rapid succession. The cap for this damage bonus is determined by Revivals. Evolve with a maxed out Tirajisú. The evolution spawns a green dragon that always deals critical hits. New relic: Green Eyes Vizard Bat Dragons will appear on the Stage Selection menu until they have been defeated at least once. They will appear on the map during a run, and they have to be activated by getting hit. Once active, time stops and enemy waves are changed until they are killed. You can fight them again in new runs, they simply won't be signaled in Stage Selection anymore after getting killed once. New Darkanas: 0 - Stake to your Heart Unlocked by defeating a Bat Dragon with Big Troubler while using the Game Killer Arcana. You will no longer be able to level up using experience gems. Instead, when defeating an enemy, they will also drop a Gold Coin, that you’ll be able to spend at a special merchant to buy weapons. Gold coins will also become your health: don't reach 0 (and quit before Red Death deals the usual 65535 damage per hit to you) New Darkanas: VIII - Edge of the Earth Unlocked by triggering a Lavatrix Machina with Para Kooleo. Gain Thorns and Move Speed locked at 200%, ignore walls, destroy light sources upon contact, and attract things that normally aren’t attracted by a Magnet, like treasure chests. New Darkanas: XIX - Heir of Fate Unlocked by surviving 15 minutes in inverse Boss Rash with Random Events and Random Level Ups enabled. While active, defeating enemies with Fire damage causes them to drop Scorched Souls. Additionally, a Nduja Fritta Tanto will trigger when the character's Health dips to a certain point. New Relics: Survarocchi Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum. Allows Survarot cards to spawn from light sources. Previously available only via the Ante Chamber dlc and a secret character, Survarots Enemahs (Secret rather than Unlockable) Unlocked by purchasing it from the Big Troubler merchant in The Lycaeum after defeating any two unique Bat Dragons. Adds an extra 18 cards based on various enemies to drafts of Survarot. For the full list of bugfixes, please see here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1794680/view/693137145499484509

1.15 FAQs

How much is 1.15? It’s a free update. Can I now share DLCs when playing online? Not yet, in this patch we managed to do the groundwork to allow for DLC sharing, but we still have to complete the feature. Can I now use Cross-save on PS and Apple+? Not yet. We still don’t have the right policies in place to do that. What platforms is update 1.15 available on? Update 1.15 is launching on Steam first. Other platforms are planned to follow by the end of the month, including Xbox, PlayStation 4/5, Nintendo Switch, Android, iOS, and Epic Games Store. Is update 1.15 coming to Nintendo Switch 2? Yes! Update 1.15 will bring Vampire Survivors to Nintendo Switch 2 for the first time. It won’t arrive at the exact same time as the other platforms, but the current plan is for Nintendo Switch 2 support to follow around two weeks after update 1.15 (but don’t hold us to that). Where are the new achievements? We will sort out the new Steam achievements in the next patch (they will pop automatically). Hey are you still updating Vampire Crawlers? Yes of course, it’s taking longer than expected to release the first QOL improvements patch and a cute looking roadmap because we got stuck for days trying to exit the game.

items.title: Vampire Crawlers Is A Vampire Survivors That's Better For Your Heart Rate
items.summary: The followup game to Vampire Survivors keeps the hook but loses some of the chaos
items.content:
I wasn’t exactly a model fan of Vampire Survivors , Poncle’s 2022 reverse bullet hell. I absolutely loved its strangely Zen blend of chaos and strategy and mindlessness, but I never got great at the strategy part. I’m not by nature a min-maxxer, and I tend to get a bit overwhelmed when a game has too many stats, instead picking some power or combo I like and sticking with it even if it isn’t ideal. So far, followup game Vampire Crawlers is giving me the same things I loved and the same things I’m less passionate about, but with a slower pace that’s helping me get more into the strategy mindset.

Vampire Crawlers (full title: Vampire Crawlers: The Turbo Wildcard From Vampire Survivors , and out now for PC and consoles) is developed with a studio called Nosebleed Interactive. You still traverse areas like a forest and a library, and you’re still levelling up all the time. But it turns Vampire Survivors into a first-person, deck-based dungeon crawler: each turn, you have a certain amount of mana to spend playing cards that can do damage, give you armor, boost your other cards, and more. As you play, you get new cards or the opportunity to tinker with your current cards to make them more powerful.

The key thing to think about here is combos, in particular the order you play your cards in. If you play them in ascending order of mana cost (0, 1, 2, etc), you’ll run up a streak that boosts the next costliest card. It’s not always the move–sometimes a nasty boss required me to ignore the combo in favor of piling on my armor, or I was me about a turn and just couldn’t resist a powerful card even if it broke my combo–but it was always on my mind as I chose my plays. This can feel a little rote at times, or at least in the early game where I still am, but I also felt like it helped guide my decision-making a little more than my long-running natural tendency to just start clicking instead of taking my time.

Like Vampire Survivors , there’s a meta-game, though this time it’s laid out in an interface charmingly stylized like a village. You can spend the gold you earn during runs on permanent power-ups and on characters with unique abilities. There’s a world of things to unlock and combine and tinker with, and I get the sense this will all become vital as the difficulty ramps up.

You could argue there’s something a little disappointing there, an encouragement to replay and grind for coins and levels that could start to drag when combined with Vampire Crawlers ’ slower pace. In Survivors , the chaos of the game distracted me from all this–every level, even if I’d seen it all before, was fast and exciting, so it never felt like I was just doing the same thing over and over, even though I was arguably doing less than I do in Crawlers . But so far, I’m finding it a good balance: Even if I’m playing a level again, I’m still excited about which cards I’ll get and which order I’ll play them in and what I can do to boost a hand. It feels like there’s a little more to do in each turn of each run, combined with the primordially satisfying flood of damage and XP. And there’s still the pleasantly thoughtless allure of “one more battle” and “one more level” that made Survivors such a particular mix of complexity and ease.

Similar to Balatro , I think one of the core appeals of Survivors and now Crawlers is sort of “breaking” the game–getting so strong and pulling down such big combos that the whole thing becomes an overpowered exercise in absurdity. It’s a strange kind of mastery when compared to other games that require more personal skill, and it’s one I find both appealing and a little hollow. I’m not sure I’ll ever have the kind of brain that will get me there before other games pull me away–the ability to develop an encyclopedic understanding of Crawlers’ trinkets and stats and combos–but so far it feels more achievable for me in Crawlers than in Survivors given its slower pace.

Vampire Crawlers keeps the core hook and essential structure of Survivors while doing its own unique thing with its own particular rhythm. I can see it joining the rotation of games I play when it’s a little too soon to go to bed, but without the adrenaline rush of Survivors that made it not great for actually going to bed. I spent the morning with it and am excited to see more of what it has to offer, even if I’m probably not the kind of person who will ever find my way to its end.

items.title: The Vampire Survivors developer is opening studios and making over 15 projects
items.summary: Poncle is opening studios in Japan and Italy as Vampire Survivors sails past 27 million players
items.content:
Playback speed × Share post Share post at current time Share from 0:00 0:00 / Generate transcript A transcript unlocks clips, previews, and editing. 16 2 The Vampire Survivors developer is opening studios and making over 15 projects Poncle is opening studios in Japan and Italy as Vampire Survivors sails past 27 million players Christopher Dring Apr 22, 2026 16 2 Share Transcript The Game Business is Live in Los Angeles on Monday, June 8, where we will be interviewing video game royalty Laura Miele, Jason Rubin and Matthew Ball live on stage. Tickets are available now.

Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube In This Edition, Poncle’s Matteo Sapio on: - Vampire Survivors spin-offs and tie-ins - Opening studios in Japan and Italy - Working on over 15 projects

During last week’s London Game Festival, I spoke with Matteo Sapio, the chief strategy officer at Vampires Survivors developer Poncle.

We were speaking in front of a live audience, and it was one of the most revealing interviews I’ve done since launching The Game Business . During out chat, Sapio announced:

That Vampire Survivors has now surpassed 27 million players

It has over 15 projects in active development (and even more in earlier stages)

It is licensing out its engine to other brands and studios to build ‘Survivors’ games based on popular IP

It has paused its third-party publishing plans

“Vampire Survivors came from a solo developer,” Sapio explains. “It was Luca Galante, who made a game for him and his friends. Vampire Survivors exploded, and in two or three months, it sold more than one million copies. Luca’s yachts are video games. So instead of buying a yacht, he made the Emerald Beyond DLC [for Vampire Survivors] with Square Enix, which we released for free. Things grew organically from there.”

For more surprising developer interviews, sign-up to The Game Business today

First, there are spin-offs to Vampire Survivors. This includes the deck-building card battler Vampire Crawlers, which is out this week.

“We [are using] the famous Vampire Survivors IP to experiment in new genres,” Sapio tells us. “We love card games, but we are not very good at card games. They’re complicated. So, we made the game that we wanted to play.”

Vampire Crawlers is out this week Second, Poncle is working on original IP. Sapio says the company is currently developing two entirely original properties.

And third , there will be a range of new ‘Survivors’ games based on other IP. These are Vampire Survivors-like games set in other universes. Some will be developed by Poncle, whereas others – such as the upcoming Warhammer Survivors – are in collaboration with other studios.

items.title: Vampire Crawlers is out now!
items.summary: Today, we are releasing Vampire Crawlers, a new spin-off set in the Vampire Survivors universe. It takes the familiar chaos of Vampire Survivors and turns it into a casual, turn-based, card-driven BLOBBER with roguelite elements. We’ve talk
items.content:
Today, we are releasing Vampire Crawlers, a new spin-off set in the Vampire Survivors universe.

It takes the familiar chaos of Vampire Survivors and turns it into a casual, turn-based, card-driven BLOBBER with roguelite elements.

We’ve talked before about wanting to take some of the accidental core pillars of Vampire Survivors and apply them to other genres: accessibility, immediacy, affordability, replayability, lightheartedness, and the usual amount of flashy nonsense. Vampire Crawlers is the first attempt at that. 

Crawl through dungeons, build busted decks, master the TurboTurn™, and try to keep the run going long enough to pretend it was all planned. You can watch the launch trailer below.

(In other news, God appears briefly and remains unhelpful.)

Vampire Crawlers

The full game includes everything from the demo, plus more content, more fixes, and more improvements across the board. The game is built around:

  • TurboTurn™ combat: Turn-based combat without the wait. Queue your moves instantly and let the game resolve them at full speed.

    [/*]

  • The Combo: cards are played in ascending mana order, and each step multiplies the next card’s effect

    [/*]

  • Wild cards that let you extend the stack and push combos further

    [/*]

  • Deckbuilding through progression: level up to gain new cards, find power-ups, chase evolutions, and customize your runs

    [/*]

  • Character cards and summoned survivors that add more effects and help create larger cascades

    [/*]

  • Dungeon exploration with treasures, floor progression, and interactive points of interest

    [/*]

  • A pace you choose yourself: take your time and be tactical, or play turns as fast as you humanly can

    [/*]

The full version also launches with the fixes and improvements made after the demo feedback period, and we are planning to keep the demo available as well.

So all of us at poncle and Nosebleed Interactive would like to say thank you to everyone who played the demo, reported bugs, shared feedback, and generally tried to break things. That was genuinely useful.

Releasing now — $9.99 / €9.99 / £9.99

You can get Vampire Crawlers on Steam by clicking the link below.

Vampire Crawlers Original Soundtrack

Also releasing into the wild: the Vampire Crawlers Original Soundtrack.

The OST includes the game’s main theme, “Il Cuor non si Spaura,” composed by Yoko Shimomura, alongside tracks by Daniele Zandara, Filippo Vicarelli, and Michael Coviello. For a total of 32 tracks and over 1 hour of music for crawling purposes, available in MP3 and FLAC on Steam. It includes both the Crawling and Turbo versions, hidden tracks that are no longer hidden, and yes, there is a disco version of the inn theme.

You can listen here:

Or download here

FAQs

  • What platforms is the game on? Vampire Crawlers is available on Steam, Nintendo Switch, Xbox, and PlayStation. Mobile versions are planned for later in 2026.

    [/*]

  • How much does it cost? £9.99 / $9.99 / €9.99 / ¥1200.

    [/*]

  • How long to beat the game? Around 20 to 30 hours, and a bit longer if you are going for every unlock.

    [/*]

  • Does the game support controllers? Yes. Controller support is included.

    [/*]

  • Does the game support cross-save between different platforms? Not right now, but we’re looking into it in time for the mobile ports.

    [/*]

  • Will save data carry over on Steam if I played the demo? Yes. Demo progress can carry over to the full game on Steam.

    [/*]

More FAQ details here: Vampire Crawlers FAQ —

https://poncle.games/vampire-crawlers-faq

See you in the next news post. Happy crawling!

-From everyone at poncle and Nosebleed Interactive
